rfc4034.title: Resource Records for the DNS Security Extensions

quotes.2.1.1: If bit 7 has value 0, then the DNSKEY record holds some other type of DNS public key and MUST NOT be used to verify RRSIGs that cover RRsets. A DNSKEY RR with the SEP set and the Zone Key flag not set MUST NOT be used to verify RRSIGs that cover RRsets.
quotes.2.1.2: The Protocol Field MUST have value 3, and the DNSKEY RR MUST be treated as invalid during signature verification if it is found to be some value other than 3.

quotes.5.3.1: The RRSIG RR's Signer's Name, Algorithm, and Key Tag fields MUST match the owner name, algorithm, and key tag for some DNSKEY RR in the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset. The matching DNSKEY RR MUST be present in the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset, and MUST have the Zone Flag bit set.
quotes.5.3.3: the public key used to verify the signature is contained in the Public Key field of the matching DNSKEY RR(s) (found in Section 5.3.1).

rfc7858.title: Specification for DNS over Transport Layer Security (TLS)

quotes.3.1: By default, a DNS client desiring privacy from DNS over TLS from a particular server MUST establish a TCP connection to port 853 on the server and MUST initiate a TLS connection.

rfc8310.title: Usage Profiles for DNS over TLS and DNS over DTLS

quotes.3: A Strict Privacy profile requires both an encrypted connection and authentication of the DNS server using an authentication domain name.
quotes.6.6: Authentication in Strict Privacy requires the DNS client to authenticate the server certificate using the authentication domain name.

fixture-binding.quote: Stable lesson-prefixed object identities are symbolic references to fixed independently verified numeric material where bound by parent. This worksheet never claims its symbolic signatures were numerically verified by an application.

patches.reason: Define the three-level crypto semantics explicitly

definitions.candidateTupleMatchAttempted: The validator compared the received RRSIG tuple (owner, type, signer, algorithm, key tag, labels, time) and candidate DNSKEY metadata (Protocol, Zone flag, SEP) against the exact reference-bound inputs. This is a symbolic/reference comparison and does not imply cryptographic execution.
definitions.eligibleKeySelected: At least one candidate passed Protocol=3 and Zone-flag eligibility and was selected for verification. Protocol!=3, Zone-flag clear (even with SEP), or no matching key means false.
definitions.conceptualVerificationInvoked: The conceptual validator invoked verification with an eligible selected key. Distinct from runtime execution; false when no eligible key is selected.
definitions.runtimeCryptographicOperationPerformed: Actual execution by the worksheet application/browser/native runtime under test. False throughout this symbolic contract; independent numeric-generator verification is a reference result, not this runtime execution.
definitions.knownMathematicalSignatureValid: Independent numeric reference result for the exact bytes, if known. It does not make an ineligible key usable and does not imply runtime execution.
definitions.signatureChecked: Contract validation decision-path completion, not a synonym for runtime crypto execution.

findings.question: Does cryptographicOperationPerformed:false mean the signature was not mathematically checked, that no eligible key was selected, or that no runtime crypto executed?
findings.resolution: Three distinct levels are required. Candidate tuple screening compares RRSIG and DNSKEY metadata against reference-bound inputs. Eligible-key selection is false for Protocol!=3, Zone-flag clear (even with SEP), signer/key mismatch or no matching key. Conceptual verification invocation is false without an eligible key. Runtime cryptographic operation is false throughout the worksheet/browser symbolic contract because no browser numeric crypto is implemented; independent numeric-generator verification is a reference result, not runtime execution. A known mathematical signature result is an independent reference result, not runtime execution, and does not make an ineligible key usable.

findings.question: Is anchorRef a raw numeric key ID or an immutable public-key artifact, and is logical-reference alpha conversion valid?
findings.resolution: anchorRef is a logical key identity string, not raw public-key bytes. Alpha conversion to the immutable public-key/DNSKEY artifact is valid only when keyId, owner, scope, flags, protocol, algorithm and exact publicKeyHex/dnskeyRdataHex match the bound keyBindings/numeric artifact. For child-ksk-g1 the binding is added explicitly; no corrected expected reference type is required. If a consumer requires an artifact-only reference, use anchorBinding rather than interpreting the keyId as bytes.

findings.question: The setup selects an established authenticated DoT channel and the checkpoint says encrypted=true/authenticatedEndpoint=resolver.example., but the upstream hop is labeled UDP. Which field is wrong?
findings.resolution: Only the transport label/input is wrong. The resolver-to-upstream hop is an established authenticated encrypted DoT channel; the stub and upstream-to-authority hops remain UDP. Per-hop query/response flags, independent trust stores and validation/security status are unchanged. No TLS handshake event or encrypted-UDP claim is added.
